- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.1), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast shows >+3% spike from prior period, reduce by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses downward trend in late period; if sentiment turns negative after peak, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +1.1, -1.1, +1.1), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2% lower than true outcome for next 2–3 periods.
